title: Monohybrid inheritance

blocks.heading: Key points
blocks.text:
| Learn | |
|---|---|
| Genotype | the alleles present, written as symbols: TT, Tt, tt |
| Tt × Tt | 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 3 dominant : 1 recessive |
| Tt × tt | 1 Tt : 1 tt |

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Genotypes, and genetic diagrams for monohybrid crosses.

blocks.heading: Genotype
blocks.text: Genotype is the genetic make-up of an organism in terms of the alleles present. It is written in allele symbols: a capital letter for the dominant allele and the same letter in lower case for the recessive allele. Tt is a genotype.

blocks.heading: Setting out a genetic diagram
blocks.text: A genetic diagram has the same lines every time. First the parental phenotypes, then the parental genotypes, then the gametes each parent can make, then every possible fertilisation, often in a grid, and finally the offspring genotypes and phenotypes with their ratio.

blocks.heading: Worked example: two heterozygous parents
blocks.text: In a pearl millet variety grown in a school garden in Ondangwa, the allele for tall stems (T) is dominant to the allele for short stems (t). Two heterozygous tall plants are crossed: Tt × Tt. Each parent makes gametes T and t. The four fertilisations give TT, Tt, Tt and tt, so the genotype ratio is 1 : 2 : 1 and the phenotype ratio is 3 tall : 1 short. If 120 seeds grow, about 120 ÷ 4 = 30 are expected to be short, and 30 × 3 = 90 tall.

blocks.heading: A heterozygous parent and a homozygous recessive parent
blocks.text: Cross a heterozygous tall plant with a short plant: Tt × tt. The tall parent makes gametes T and t; the short parent makes only t. The offspring are Tt and tt in the ratio 1 : 1, so about half are tall and half are short. Ratios like these predict proportions: a small number of offspring can differ from them by chance.

blocks.heading: Genotype is not phenotype
blocks.text: In a genetic diagram, the parents are written as genotypes, pairs of allele symbols such as Tt and tt. Words such as tall and short are phenotypes. They belong on the phenotype lines and never replace the genotypes.
